summary: Returns the value after checking that it is not a number with a fractional part.
description: A synonym of the `Float` family, offered under the name people reach for first. In JavaScript every number already is a double, so `double` names no runtime distinction of its own.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, with a number with a fractional part excluded from its type.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is a number with a fractional part.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireNonDouble(42); // => 42
requireNonDouble(1.0); // => 1.0
requireNonDouble(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonDouble(-0.1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
